title: Web Application Error Rate
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Web Application Error Rate' only. Does not supplant organization-wide SIEM playbooks for unrelated threat classes or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `soc_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `security_infra_web_application_error_rate` (UC-10.13.38), SOC dashboard panel "Security Infra — Web Application Error Rate", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:soc_controls.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **SOC tuning or purple-team exercise** — Expected alert volume during rule validation for 'Web Application Error Rate'. Match active CHG with `purple_team=true`.

2. **Content deployment window** — TA or CIM update shifts field extractions on `index=security` `configured sourcetype`.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Web CIM.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `status=500`, `url`.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Group by `app` token in URL path; tie to deployment markers.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=security tag=web status>=500
| timechart span=5m count by url
| where count>100
```

Understanding this SPL

**Web Application Error Rate** — Application-level errors in `status` 500 series or custom `error` field in CIM extensions.

Documented **Data sources**: `status=500`, `url`. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Web CIM. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: security.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=security, tags. Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `timechart` plots the metric over time using **span=5m** buckets with a separate series **by url** — ideal for trending and alerting on this use case.
• Filters the current rows with `where count>100` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.

Optional CIM / accelerated variant (same use case, normalized fields via Common Information Model):

```spl
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.status>=500 by Web.url, _time span=5m
```

Understanding this CIM / accelerated SPL

**Web Application Error Rate** — Application-level errors in `status` 500 series or custom `error` field in CIM extensions.

Documented **Data sources**: `status=500`, `url`. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Web CIM. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

This **CIM or accelerated** block uses normalized field names and/or `tstats` over data models. Enable **acceleration** on the referenced models (and correct CIM knowledge objects) or the search may return nothing.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Uses `tstats` against accelerated summaries for data model `Web.Web` — enable acceleration for that model.

Enable Data Model Acceleration (and metric indexes for `mstats`) for the models or datasets referenced above; otherwise `tstats`/`mstats` may return no results from summaries.


Step 3 — Validate
Accelerate the CIM data model used in the optional tstats path, then run both the primary and `cimSpl` searches over a week that includes a known good baseline. Spot-check a few rows and tune thresholds; confirm no permission or tagging gap is hiding part of the population.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Line chart (5xx by app), Table (top paths).

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Web CIM — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into security. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`status, url`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We use the same kind of check described for "Web Application Error Rate" once our data is shaped in a common, repeatable way across products. We help the team see trouble early, compare different tools fairly, and avoid building a one-off report for every vendor.
